name: Bite off more than you can chew

meaning.zh:
“贪多嚼不烂” 或 “能力不及欲望”。

这个短语起源于19世纪的美国。它原本用来描述一个人咬下比自己能咀嚼的更多的食物，后来引申为采取超过自己能力范围内的任务或职责。如今，这个idiom常用于形容一个人承担了超过自己能力范围的工作或责任，难以应付。
meaning.en: This phrase originates in 19th-century America. It was initially used to describe a person taking a bite of more food than they could chew, and later evolved to mean taking on tasks or responsibilities that exceed one's capability. Today, this idiom is commonly used to describe someone who has undertaken more work or responsibilities than they can handle.

lines.en: John realized he had bitten off more than he could chew when he volunteered for all those projects.
lines.zh: 约翰自愿接下所有那些项目后才意识到自己贪多嚼不烂。

lines.en: She tends to bite off more than she can chew at work.
lines.zh: 她在工作上总是贪多嚼不烂。

lines.en: Don't bite off more than you can chew; take on one project at a time.
lines.zh: 不要贪多嚼不烂；一次只做一个项目。
